affect.d: To have an influence on someone or something; to change it.
affect.ex: Lack of sleep can seriously affect your concentration during the exam.

effect.d: A change or result that something causes.
effect.ex: The new policy had a positive effect on air quality in the city.

accept.d: To agree to take something that is offered, or to agree that something is true.
accept.ex: The university was happy to accept her application.

except.ex: The library is open every day except Sunday.

advice.cue: noun (UK c) - an opinion about what to do
advice.d: An opinion that you give someone about what they should do.
advice.ex: My teacher gave me some useful advice about the writing test.

advise.d: To tell someone what you think they should do.
advise.ex: Doctors advise people to drink plenty of water in hot weather.

device.d: A piece of equipment or a tool made for a particular purpose.
device.ex: Please switch off every electronic device before the test begins.

devise.d: To invent a plan, system or method by careful thought.
devise.ex: The council must devise a better way to reduce traffic in the centre.

practice.cue: noun (UK c) - repeated exercise; a doctor's business
practice.d: Regular repeated activity in order to improve a skill; also the business of a doctor or lawyer.
practice.ex: With regular practice, your listening score will improve.

practise.cue: verb (UK s) - to do repeatedly to improve
practise.d: To do something regularly in order to become better at it.
practise.ex: You should practise spelling for fifteen minutes every day.

licence.d: An official document that gives you permission to do or own something.
licence.ex: You need a valid driving licence to rent a car.

license.cue: verb (UK s) - to give official permission
license.d: To give official permission for someone to do or sell something.
license.ex: The city will only license a small number of new taxis this year.

principal.cue: main; the head of a school
principal.d: Most important or main; also the head of a school or college.
principal.ex: The principal reason for the delay was the bad weather.

principle.cue: noun - a basic rule or belief
principle.d: A basic truth, rule or belief that guides behaviour or explains how something works.
principle.ex: Equal access to education is an important principle of a fair society.

complement.cue: something that completes or goes well with
complement.d: To add to something in a way that makes it complete or better.
complement.ex: The online course is designed to complement classroom teaching.

compliment.d: A polite remark that praises someone.
compliment.ex: The examiner paid her a compliment on her pronunciation.

stationary.ex: The bus was stationary at the traffic lights when the accident happened.

stationery.cue: noun - paper, pens, envelopes (e for envelope)
stationery.d: Paper, pens, envelopes and other materials used for writing.
stationery.ex: Students can buy stationery at the shop next to the library.

lose.cue: verb - to fail to keep (one o)
lose.d: To no longer have something, or to fail to win.
lose.ex: Do not lose your receipt, because you will need it for a refund.

loose.d: Not firmly fixed or not fitting tightly.
loose.ex: One of the screws on the bookshelf is loose.

whether.d: Used to talk about a choice between two or more possibilities.
whether.ex: The students must decide whether to live on campus or rent a flat.

weather.d: The conditions in the air, such as temperature, rain and wind, at a particular time.
weather.ex: The trip was cancelled because of the stormy weather.

their.d: Belonging to or connected with them.
their.ex: The visitors left their luggage at the reception desk.

there.d: In, at or to that place; also used to say that something exists.
there.ex: There are three bedrooms in the apartment.

they're.ex: They're planning to visit the museum on Saturday.

than.ex: Train tickets are cheaper than plane tickets for this route.

then.d: At that time, or after that.
then.ex: Fill in the form and then hand it to the receptionist.

quiet.ex: Please keep quiet in the reading room.

quite.d: Fairly but not very; or completely.
quite.ex: The test was quite difficult, but I finished on time.

desert.cue: noun - a dry sandy area (one s)
desert.d: A large, dry area of land with very little rain and few plants.
desert.ex: Very few plants can survive in the desert without water.

dessert.cue: noun - sweet food after a meal (two s, like 'sweet stuff')
dessert.d: Sweet food eaten at the end of a meal.
dessert.ex: The restaurant offers fruit salad for dessert.

council.d: A group of people elected to make decisions for a town or area.
council.ex: The local council has built a new recycling centre.

counsel.d: Advice, especially from a professional; to give such advice.
counsel.ex: The university offers free counsel to students who feel stressed.

economic.d: Connected with trade, industry and money in a country.
economic.ex: The country has seen strong economic growth over the past decade.

economical.d: Using money, fuel or time carefully without waste.
economical.ex: Small cars are more economical to run than large ones.

historic.ex: The signing of the agreement was a historic moment for both nations.

historical.d: Connected with the past or with the study of history.
historical.ex: The museum has a large collection of historical documents.

lead.cue: verb (present) - to guide; noun - a grey metal
lead.d: To show the way or to be in control of a group.
lead.ex: A guide will lead the group through the old town.

led.d: Past tense and past participle of 'lead'.
led.ex: The new law led to a sharp fall in road accidents.

past.d: The time before now; or going beyond something.
past.ex: In the past, most people in the village worked on farms.

passed.d: Past tense of 'pass': went by, or succeeded in a test.
passed.ex: She passed the exam with a band score of eight.

breath.cue: noun - air taken in (short e sound)
breath.d: The air that goes into and out of your lungs.
breath.ex: Take a deep breath before you start speaking.

breathe.cue: verb - to take air in (long ee sound, final e)
breathe.d: To take air into your lungs and let it out again.
breathe.ex: Trees help us breathe cleaner air in cities.

cloth.cue: noun - material made from cotton, wool etc.
cloth.d: Material made by weaving cotton, wool or other fibres.
cloth.ex: The bags are made of strong cotton cloth.

clothes.d: Things such as shirts and trousers that you wear.
clothes.ex: Pack warm clothes because the nights are cold.

cite.d: To mention something as an example or as evidence, or to quote a source.
cite.ex: In academic writing you must cite the sources you use.

site.cue: noun - a place or location; a website
site.d: A place where something is, was or will be built; also a website.
site.ex: The site of the new hospital is close to the station.

sight.cue: noun - the ability to see; something seen
sight.d: The ability to see, or something that you see.
sight.ex: The old castle is the most famous sight in the city.

raise.cue: verb + object - to lift or increase something
raise.d: To lift something or to increase an amount or level.
raise.ex: The government plans to raise taxes on fuel.

rise.cue: verb, no object - to go up
rise.ex: Sea levels continue to rise because of global warming.

emigrate.d: To leave your own country to live permanently in another.
emigrate.ex: Many young graduates emigrate in search of better jobs.

immigrate.cue: to come into a new country (im = in)
immigrate.d: To come into a foreign country to live there permanently.
immigrate.ex: Her grandparents decided to immigrate to Canada in the 1970s.

ensure.d: To make certain that something happens.
ensure.ex: Please ensure that your name is written on every page.

insure.d: To buy insurance so that you receive money if something is lost or damaged.
insure.ex: It is wise to insure your laptop before you travel.

assure.cue: to tell someone confidently to remove doubt
assure.d: To tell someone that something is definitely true so that they do not worry.
assure.ex: I can assure you that your booking has been confirmed.

personal.d: Belonging to or connected with a particular person.
personal.ex: Do not share your personal details with strangers online.

personnel.cue: noun - the staff of an organisation
personnel.d: The people who work for an organisation.
personnel.ex: All medical personnel must wear a badge.

precede.d: To happen or exist before something else.
precede.ex: A short introduction will precede the main lecture.

proceed.cue: to go forward, continue (one of three -ceed words)
proceed.d: To continue or to move forward.
proceed.ex: Passengers should proceed to gate twelve.

adverse.d: Having a harmful or negative effect.
adverse.ex: The medicine can have adverse effects on some patients.

averse.d: Strongly disliking or opposed to something.
averse.ex: He is not averse to working at the weekend.

discreet.d: Careful not to cause embarrassment or attract attention.
discreet.ex: The hotel staff were polite and discreet.

discrete.cue: separate, distinct (the t separates the two e's)
discrete.ex: The course is divided into four discrete modules.

eminent.d: Famous and respected in a particular field.
eminent.ex: The lecture was given by an eminent scientist.

imminent.ex: Forecasters warned that a storm was imminent.

allusion.d: Something that is said or written that refers to a subject indirectly.
allusion.ex: The speech contained an allusion to a famous poem.

illusion.d: A false idea or belief, or something that looks real but is not.
illusion.ex: Mirrors can create the illusion of a larger room.

aloud.cue: out loud, in a voice people can hear
aloud.d: In a voice that other people can hear.
aloud.ex: The teacher asked him to read the paragraph aloud.

allowed.ex: Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.

fair.cue: just and reasonable; an outdoor event
fair.d: Treating people equally; or a public event with stalls and rides.
fair.ex: It is not fair to charge students more than other visitors.

fare.d: The money you pay to travel on a bus, train, plane or taxi.
fare.ex: The bus fare to the airport is four pounds.

whole.ex: We spent the whole afternoon in the science museum.

hole.d: An empty space or an opening in something.
hole.ex: There is a hole in the fence around the garden.

peace.d: A situation with no war or violence; calm and quiet.
peace.ex: The two countries signed a peace agreement.

piece.cue: a part of something (a piece of pie)
piece.d: A part or bit of something.
piece.ex: Write your answer on a separate piece of paper.

plain.d: Simple, without decoration; or a large area of flat land.
plain.ex: The flat plain was perfect for growing wheat.

plane.d: An aircraft; or a flat surface.
plane.ex: Our plane landed at Heathrow two hours late.

role.d: The position or purpose that someone or something has.
role.ex: Parents play an important role in a child's education.

roll.cue: to turn over and over; a small bread; a list
roll.d: To move by turning over and over; also a small loaf of bread.
roll.ex: The ball began to roll down the hill.

sole.cue: only; the bottom of a foot or shoe
sole.d: Only; or the bottom surface of a foot or shoe.
sole.ex: Tourism is the sole source of income for the island.

soul.d: The spiritual part of a person; also deep feeling.
soul.ex: The singer performed with great heart and soul.

waist.d: The middle part of the body above the hips.
waist.ex: The trousers were too big around the waist.

waste.d: Material that is no longer wanted; or to use something carelessly.

weak.ex: His listening was strong but his spelling was weak.

wear.cue: to have clothes on your body
wear.d: To have clothes, shoes or jewellery on your body.
wear.ex: Visitors must wear a helmet on the building site.

where.ex: Could you tell me where the post office is?

moral.d: Connected with the difference between right and wrong.
moral.ex: Scientists face moral questions about genetic research.

morale.cue: confidence and enthusiasm of a group
morale.d: The amount of confidence and enthusiasm that a group of people feel.
morale.ex: Staff morale improved after the pay rise.

formerly.ex: The art gallery was formerly a power station.

formally.cue: in a formal or official way
formally.d: In a formal, polite or official way.
formally.ex: The new library will be formally opened next month.

altogether.ex: The tickets cost sixty pounds altogether.

already.cue: before now, earlier than expected (one word)
already.d: Before now, or earlier than expected.
already.ex: I have already paid the deposit.

everyday.ex: Smartphones have become part of everyday life.

maybe.ex: Maybe we should book the tickets online.

dependant.cue: noun (UK) - a person who depends on you
dependant.d: A person, especially a child, who depends on someone else for money and support.
dependant.ex: Applicants must list every dependant who will travel with them.

dependent.d: Needing the help or support of someone or something.
dependent.ex: The region is heavily dependent on tourism.

storey.cue: noun (UK) - a level of a building
storey.d: A level or floor of a building.
storey.ex: The new library is a five-storey building.

story.cue: noun - a description of events, a tale
story.d: A description of real or imaginary events.
story.ex: The children listened to a story about a brave fox.

programme.cue: noun (UK) - a TV show, a plan of events, a course
programme.d: A show on television or radio, or a planned series of activities.
programme.ex: The exchange programme lasts for one academic year.

program.d: A set of instructions that makes a computer do a task.
program.ex: The program crashed while I was saving the file.

tyre.cue: noun (UK) - the rubber ring on a wheel
tyre.d: A thick rubber ring that fits around the wheel of a car or bicycle.
tyre.ex: We stopped at the garage to repair a flat tyre.

tire.d: To become tired, or to make someone tired.
tire.ex: Long journeys tire young children quickly.

cheque.cue: noun (UK) - a printed bank payment form
cheque.d: A printed form that you sign and use to pay money from your bank account.
cheque.ex: The landlord prefers payment by cheque or bank transfer.

check.d: To examine something to make sure it is correct or safe.
check.ex: Always check your spelling before you hand in your answer sheet.

metre.d: A unit for measuring length, equal to 100 centimetres.
metre.ex: The swimming pool is twenty-five metres long.

meter.cue: noun - a device that measures (gas meter, parking meter)
meter.d: A device that measures and records an amount, such as of gas or electricity.
meter.ex: Someone will come to read the electricity meter on Monday.

draught.cue: noun (UK) - a current of cold air
draught.d: A current of unpleasant cold air in a room.
draught.ex: Close the window - there is a terrible draught.

draft.cue: a first version of a text
draft.d: A piece of writing that is not yet in its finished form.
draft.ex: Write a quick draft first and then improve it.

disc.cue: noun (UK) - a flat round object; CD
disc.d: A flat, round object; also a CD or DVD.
disc.ex: The film is available on disc and online.

disk.d: A device for storing computer information.
disk.ex: Save a copy of your essay on the hard disk.

its.d: Belonging to or connected with a thing, animal or idea.
its.ex: The company announced its plans for expansion.

it's.d: Short form of 'it is' or 'it has'.
it's.ex: It's important to read the instructions carefully.

your.d: Belonging to or connected with you.
your.ex: Please write your full name in capital letters.

you're.ex: You're allowed to use a pencil in the listening test.

whose.d: Used to ask or say who something belongs to.
whose.ex: Whose bag is this on the chair?

who's.d: Short form of 'who is' or 'who has'.
who's.ex: Who's going to give the presentation tomorrow?

to.d: Used to show direction, or before a verb (to go).
to.ex: We walked to the station together.

too.d: Also; or more than is needed or wanted.
too.ex: The room was too small for twenty students.

two.cue: the number 2 (w as in twin, twice)
two.ex: The flat has two bedrooms and a small kitchen.
